title: Two High-Speed Trains Collide in Central Spain, Killing at Least 64
dek: A Renfe and an Iryo train collided on the Madrid-Seville line near Urda on Wednesday morning, the deadliest high-speed rail crash in Spain since 2013 and the second on the same route this year.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: A Renfe high-speed AVE train, class 100, at a station platform

keyPoints: A Renfe train and an Iryo train collided near Urda, in Spain's Castilla-La Mancha region, on the Madrid-Seville high-speed line on Wednesday morning.
Reports put the death toll at no fewer than 64 to 68, with dozens more injured and officials warning the count could rise.
Officials say the Renfe train probably struck the Iryo train from behind, derailing two Iryo carriages down an embankment.
It is the second deadly high-speed crash on this line in 2026, after a January collision near Adamuz that killed 46.
body:
Two high-speed trains collided on Spain's Madrid-Seville line on Wednesday morning near the town of Urda in the Castilla-La Mancha region, killing dozens of people in one of the country's worst rail disasters in more than a decade.

Reuters reported that at least 64 people were killed and 80 injured, citing a spokesperson for the regional government. ABC News, citing the regional president, reported that at least 68 people had died and said the toll was expected to rise. The two figures reflect a count that was still changing when the reports were filed, and Meridian will update this story if officials confirm a new total.

## What happened

The collision happened at about 8:30 a.m. local time at kilometer marker 118, according to ABC News, which cited Spain's Transport Ministry. A Renfe train and an Iryo train, both travelling from Madrid to Seville, were involved. Reuters placed the crash just after 9 a.m.

The Iryo train was carrying 146 passengers, including one baby, and the Renfe train had 397, according to the ministry figures cited by ABC. Preliminary findings suggest the Renfe train struck the Iryo train from behind, causing two Iryo coaches to derail and fall down an embankment. Regional authorities said 24 of the people killed were found on the Renfe train and the rest on the Iryo train.

## Rescue and response

Firefighters and military emergency units were dispatched to the scene, and rescue crews were using dogs to search the wreckage, according to regional officials. ABC reported that at least 15 people were seriously injured and more than 50 others were hospitalized with lesser injuries. Hospitals in Toledo and Alcazar de San Juan prepared to receive patients and issued appeals for blood donations, according to Hungarian Conservative.

Castilla-La Mancha president Emiliano Garcia-Page and Transport Minister Oscar Puente travelled to the scene. Garcia-Page told reporters that "All of Spain is mourning" and said the ministry would try to determine how the crash happened. Rail service between Madrid and Seville was suspended after the collision, according to Hungarian Conservative.

## A second crash on the same line

The crash is the second major high-speed rail accident in Spain this year involving the same operators and the same line. In January, an Iryo and a Renfe train collided near Adamuz in the province of Cordoba, killing 46 people, according to ABC. Regional officials said the two accidents appeared to have unrelated causes, though an independent investigation will be needed to confirm that.

ABC described the Urda crash as the deadliest high-speed train accident in Spain since 2013, when 80 people died after a train derailed in Galicia.

## What comes next

Garcia-Page said the investigation should be carried out by the independent railway accident investigation commission. He also said that if safety systems need to be strengthened to restore public confidence, the government will act. Regional officials said investigators would examine whether there were any failures in the safety system.

For now, the most important facts are the confirmed count of dead and injured, the cause of the impact, and the status of rail service between Madrid and Seville. Meridian will update this story as officials release new information.
